transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Greene (Redwood CSM), Jared Kline (LyricLabs CTO), Priya Menon (Head of Search), Evan Torres (Infra), Samira Ali (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Discussed embedding dims vs throughput, fanout + rerank cost, Dedicated capacity for tail-latency, VPC peering and KMS requirements. Agreed pilot: 2-week dedicated smoke test + data share.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros then we'll jump into the use case.
00:12 Jared: Hey yes, thanks. I'm Jared, CTO at LyricLabs, we run a music recommendation and editorial search product. Priya's on the search side, Evan infrastruc, Samira model ops.
00:25 Maya: Awesome. Ravi and I will walk through hosting options and then dig into the rerank flow. Quick ask — what are your throughput and latency targets?
00:38 Priya: Target is roughly 120 qps peak for retrieval queries, typical median p50 should be < 120ms end-to-end for reranked results. P95 ideally under 400ms. We also do daily batch re-indexing across ~20M docs.
00:57 Ravi: Got it. When you say 120 qps, is that retrieval fanout per query? Like how many candidates do you usually fetch before reranking?
01:06 Priya: Good question. Current pipeline: embed query, ANN search gives ~1k candidates from Milvus, then a BERT-based reranker reduces to top 10. But we want to explore lower fanouts for cost. Sometimes we do 256 or 512 candidates.
01:20 Samira: Our current embedding dim is 1024, produced offline with a transformer embedder. We have experimented with 512 and 256 and saw small quality drops but big cost wins.
01:33 Maya: This is perfect. I want to frame two levers: A) where to host the embedding + rerank (Hosted API vs Dedicated GPU pool vs Private VPC/on-prem) and B) architecture: high-dim embeddings + large fanout vs compact embeddings + rerank more heavily. Each has latency/cost/accuracy tradeoffs.
01:50 Ravi: Also important: whether we do rerank on Redwood or keep reranker in your infra and have Redwood just serve efficient embeddings or generation. Either can work.
01:59 Evan: For security we require SOC2, KMS-integrated key management for any PII-ish vectors, VPC peering if we go with Dedicated, and audit logs.
02:10 Maya: Redwood supports SOC2, SSO/SAML, and KMS integrations. Dedicated has VPC/private networking options and Private (on-prem) gives full control if you need it air-gapped. We'll include our compliance pack.
02:22 Noah: I'll drop the security pack link in the follow-up along with the pricing model.

02:35 Speaker 1: (unclear) ok so the big question is latency at scale.
02:41 Ravi: Right. Let's walk latency model. If you do embedding search with 1k fanout at 1024 dims then rerank with a transformer (student/bert reranker), cost per q will be dominated by reranker inference. With Dedicated we can pin GPU and get lower tail latency; with Hosted you may see more variability but faster time-to-value.
03:05 Priya: We want predictable p95, that's why we leaned Dedicated in previous pilots. But we also want Redwood to show the unit economics vs our current Milvus cluster.
03:15 Maya: For predictability we often recommend Dedicated for production rerank at your scale. Hosted is great for early experiments and mixed traffic but Dedicated's isolation helps with steady tail latency. Private would be if you want control over keys and network beyond Dedicated VPC options.

03:30 Evan: What about hybrid search? We may want an L2 fallback to a cheaper embedding model for cold queries. Any way to route by score/latency?
03:40 Ravi: Yes — Redwood supports routing policies. You can route by cost, latency, or model quality. A common approach: a compact embedding (256-d) index for most traffic, fall back to higher-d 1024 for hard queries or low-confidence matches, or run reranker only for top-K candidates.
03:57 Samira: How does caching factor? We have lot of repeated queries for popular tracks.
04:03 Maya: We have automatic prefix and embedding-level caching; for retrieval we can cache embeddings and ANN results, cutting compute and vector DB calls. Also caching plays well with TTL policies.
04:14 Jared: Ok. Can you walk a little through the benchmark plan you mentioned? We want to understand how you'd validate p95 under our workload.
04:22 Ravi: Sure. Typical benchmark steps: 1) you share a sample dataset + traffic trace; 2) we run a smoke test with 1k docs locally to validate quality; 3) scale to a representative subset with synthetic traffic to reproduce 120 qps peak and measure p50/p95. For rerank we include warm-up runs to populate caches and KV. We'll report latency distributions and cost per thousand queries.
04:42 Priya: Do you run the ANN layer or can we keep Milvus? We have index tuning in Milvus that took a while.
04:50 Ravi: You can keep Milvus and have Redwood perform embedding generation and rerank — typical hybrid. Alternatively, Redwood can host the ANN index (we've integrated with HNSW-based indexes) as part of Dedicated. Integration is flexible.
05:03 Evan: If we keep Milvus, how do you handle network egress and VPC? We can't expose internal indices publicly.
05:11 Maya: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering or private link so traffic stays inside your cloud. For Hosted with sensitive data we recommend using Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.

05:25 Jared: Let's talk numbers — assume 120 qps peak, 1k fanout, rerank model costs 8ms/token? (rough estimate). What does that translate to in capacity?
05:36 Ravi: If the reranker is GPU-accelerated and you batch requests, you can handle higher throughput. But rerankers are often the bottleneck because they evaluate many pairs. Practical approaches: reduce fanout to 256 and rely on stronger embeddings, or use distilled rerankers optimized for throughput. Also quantization can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput.
05:56 Samira: We've tried distillation but accuracy dropped at tail queries. Is there an eval strategy you recommend?
06:02 Ravi: We tie quality monitoring to prompt/eval sets. For rerank, we suggest an embedding + rerank A/B test: run both 512-d + 512-fanout and 1024-d + 256-fanout, compare nDCG@10 and latency/cost. Redwood Optimize can surface regressions across defined eval sets.
06:23 Priya: We'd like to see concrete cost comparisons — e.g., cost per million reranked queries across hosting options.
06:29 Maya: We'll prepare a cost model: Hosted per embedding + per-rerank token cost; Dedicated amortized monthly node cost normalized to qps; Private is licensing + infra. We'll include a scenario for 100k daily active queries and peak 120 qps.

06:45 Speaker 2: How do you handle model versioning and rollouts for rerank models?
06:49 Ravi: Redwood has model versioning and rollout features — canary/A-B and automatic fallback to previous model if quality or latency regressions are detected. You pin model versions for dedicated pools.
06:59 Evan: Any opinion on embedding dim for our music domain — 256, 512, or 1024? We're worried about cold-artist queries and long tail.
07:09 Samira: Music embedding semantics can be subtle — artist/genre metadata plus lyric embeddings. We use multi-vector per document sometimes.
07:18 Ravi: If you use multi-vector per doc, vector DB fanout complexity increases. Often 512 is a good compromise for catalog scale ~20M. 1024 gives better nearest-neighbor recall but increases index size and search CPU. For rerank heavy approach maybe 512 + 512-fanout then rerank top10 gives good economics.
07:34 Maya: Also consider sparse/hybrid features — keyword signals combined with dense embeddings reduce fanout needs.

07:44 Priya: Security again: audit logs and KMS are blockers for enterprise customers. Can you confirm audit retention and KMS provider compatibility?
07:53 Maya: Our audit logs can be exported to your SIEM; retention tiers are configurable. For KMS we integrate with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and support HSM for Private deployments. We'll include the specific mappings in the security pack.
08:06 Jared: Good. About pilot scope — we prefer a short dedicated pilot that runs with real traffic but capped capacity. What's typical?
08:14 Ravi: Usually a 2-week pilot: week 1 ingest & smoke test, week 2 run traffic ramp and measure latency/quality. We can run in Hosted for speed or spin up Dedicated reserved capacity for more realistic tail latency. For your p95 requirements I'd recommend Dedicated pilot so we can pin nodes and simulate steady-state.
08:33 Priya: Any SLA during pilot?
08:36 Maya: Pilot SLAs are softer, but if you move to Dedicated contract we can include contractual latency and uptime targets. We'll also provide DRI support during the pilot.

08:47 Evan: Are there limitations on batch sizes or KV cache sizes? We have large prefix caches.
08:53 Ravi: Limits exist per node based on memory. For Dedicated you can choose larger GPU/mem instances and adjust cache TTL. We can provide recommended configs based on your traffic trace.

09:05 Samira: Regarding our reranker, it's an in-house BERT variant. Would you run that model in Redwood or do you prefer serving it from our infra?
09:14 Ravi: We can host your reranker in Redwood Dedicated if you provide the model container or ONNX. If you prefer to keep it in your infra we can call out to it but that adds network hop and may affect p95. Hosting in Dedicated is lower latency.
09:27 Priya: How do you handle embedding updates and re-indexing 20M docs?
09:32 Maya: We support incremental reindexing and background re-embed jobs. For large-scale reindex you can run offline jobs and stream updates; we also support snapshot-based bulk ingestion to accelerate initial builds.

09:44 Jared: Let's talk costs in a ballpark — not exact numbers — but how does Dedicated amortized cost compare to Hosted per qps?
09:52 Maya: Ballpark: Hosted is typically higher per-unit but zero infra ops; Dedicated has fixed monthly cost so for sustained traffic it becomes cheaper. We'll model both cases in the pricing doc.
10:03 Priya: Also curious about quantization — can you use int8/4 quantized rerankers without large accuracy loss?
10:09 Ravi: Many rerankers tolerate 8-bit quantization using quant-aware tuning; 4-bit is trickier but possible with certain kernels. We'll include quantization recommendations for your model family.

10:22 Speaker 3: (background) what about monitoring and observability?
10:25 Noah: Redwood Console gives per-route latency and cost breakdown, token-level cost, and model-level dashboards. You can set alerts on p95 and quality regressions. We'll share screenshots in the follow-up.

10:36 Priya: We want to see the dashboard and an example of rollback after a regression.
10:40 Ravi: We'll demo rollback in the technical kickoff. We can show canary metrics and automatic fallback policy.

10:52 Samira: On evaluation metrics, we want nDCG@10 and recall@100 plus business metrics like CTR lift. Can Redwood report custom metrics?
10:59 Maya: Yes, Redwood can ingest custom eval metrics tied to an eval set and flag regressions. Redwood Optimize will warn on model quality drift.

11:12 Jared: Anything else blocking? We want to make sure the pilot doesn't require too much lift from our infra.
11:19 Maya: For pilot we'll ask for a 1k doc sample and a 24h trace. We'll do the heavy lifting for infra. If you want Dedicated pilot we'll request VPC peering and the usual security forms.
11:30 Evan: Timeline: security review might take 2 weeks. Is that ok?
11:34 Maya: Yes we can parallelize. We'll get pricing and benchmark plan to you while security reviews.

11:42 Priya: Are there any gotchas with multi-vector docs?
11:46 Ravi: Multi-vector increases candidate size; shard routing and dedup at query time help. We recommend normalizing vectors per subtype and testing different recall strategies during the pilot.
11:56 Speaker 1: (brief) ok thanks that helps.
11:59 Maya: Great. Let's recap next steps.
12:02 Maya: Action items: I'll send pricing + SLA and security pack. Ravi will send benchmark plan and list of artifact formats we need. Jared's team will share sample docs and traces. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff.
12:14 Jared: Sounds good. Looking forward to the pricing by next week.
12:18 Priya: We'll aim to get docs over by Thursday.
12:21 Maya: Perfect. Noah will include links in the follow-up. Thanks everyone.
12:27 End of call.

Notes on transcript tone: occasional mis-attributed lines (Speaker 1/2/3), filler language, and transcription artifacts present (e.g., "infrastruc"), and some technical nouns slightly off (e.g., "HNSW-based indexes" spelled correctly sometimes, sometimes missing). The content contains realistic sales qualification, security gating, pilot plan, and concrete next steps.
